[measurement]{.chip .measured} [decision]{.chip .decision} [negative result]{.chip .negative} Entry 42 · milestone M4
:::

M4 asks three different questions: what the networks can be proved to do throughout an
input box, whether calibrated intervals cover held-out reference outputs, and how closely
the coupled simulation follows the physics code. The owner has chosen the properties and
tolerances. This continuation writes those contracts and checks the existing transport runs.

**Making proofs reproducible.** The owner approved storing the selected models and explicit
input boxes with the code, so CI can access them. A hash manifest checks the stored files;
it is not a proof certificate. The owner also approved auto_LiRPA, the bounding engine, with
input-box splitting. The full alpha,beta-CROWN package remains a fallback if needed.

**Copies for the verifier.** The new PyTorch exporters reproduce preprocessing, each member
network and the physical output transforms. Two averaging details matter: transport averages
in signed-log space before mapping back to flux; EC averages raw outputs before applying its
physical clamps. Strict relative-only comparison exposed rounding near zero, also present
between eager and compiled JAX. The owner approved an explicit mixed floating-point
criterion, and [13 export checks pass in each mode: all selected members, random box points, local holdouts, physical transforms and served means, with rtol=1e-12 and atol=1e-12 in each declared output unit]{.claim}[C-180](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-180){.cid .st-tested}. No formal proof is claimed by numerical parity.

**Properties written down.** [six property contracts load; 14 property-validation tests pass in each mode, including malformed-domain, tolerance and output-schema rejection]{.claim}[C-177](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-177){.cid .st-tested}. The contracts name the model, output units,
domain source, statement and owner decision. A loader rejects incomplete or malformed
contracts. Passing these software checks means the contracts can be read reliably, not that
their statements have been proved.

**The coupled transport check.** The saved matched runs provide a result without a new
compute job. Temperatures live at cell centres; the guard says which faces the surrogate
serves. Both profiles are interpolated onto those same served faces before comparing them.
The full-profile errors and a conservative cell restriction are also retained.

| machine | served-face comparison with TGLF | result |
|---|---|---|
| ITER | [served-face T_e 7.42%, T_i 8.18%, both passing the 15% limit; whole profile 7.72/9.23%; 34 of 51 final-state faces served]{.claim}[C-178](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-178){.cid .st-measured} | passes the chosen limit |
| MAST-U | [served-face T_e 35.33%, T_i 49.15%, both failing 15%; whole profile 41.51/62.39%; cells with both adjacent faces served give 11.86/23.24%, still failing T_i; 13 of 26 final-state faces served]{.claim}[C-179](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-179){.cid .st-measured} | fails the chosen limit |

The MAST-U result becomes ceiling [K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030). Selecting only cells with two served adjacent faces
still leaves ion temperature outside the limit. The final-state mask does not count every
fallback call during the run. No tolerance was changed.

The owner prioritized MAST-U remediation before further proofs and calibration. The failed
accuracy criterion remains explicit, with its tolerance unchanged. The
[M4 page](../milestones/M4.qmd) records the work still required.
